title: Cast iron smelting in ancient China
summary: Chinese ironworkers were casting iron by the 5th century BC or earlier, and cast iron was used widely in farming, warfare and crafts. Researchers note that iron production in the Central Plains has been largely based on cast iron smelting since about then. A forced air blast, furnace design and the bronze-casting tradition lay behind the shift from bloomery iron to cast iron.

uncertainty.note: Han and Chen: invention occurred during the 5th century BC or earlier. 5th century BC converted to astronomical years -499 to -400; "or earlier" is why the start range extends back. Cast iron fragments from Tianma-Qucun and a Liuhe tomb are mentioned as earlier (8th century BC) but it is unclear whether they were intentional.

importance.justification: Early cast iron allowed widespread iron tools and weapons in China, which the sources link to farming and state power.
